title: The Cold Case Girl
logline: A famous true-crime podcaster built her name reopening cold cases where women were failed by the system — but the reader knows what her listeners don't: when the law can't touch a guilty man, she finishes the case herself. Her newest target is the most dangerous yet, because he's the one person who has figured out exactly what she is.

chapter_map.beat: Nadia finishes a target cleanly (reader learns she kills); podcast fame as cover; a detail suggests someone watched.
The kill lands publicly as an "accident"; Nadia performs grief on-air; plant the watcher thread.
New case opens — cold-case murder of Elise Marchetti; Nadia announces it; the guilty man Victor Rhodes walks free, untouchable.
Nadia activates her network (lawyer, coroner, hacker); first evidence gathered; establish her rules.
Nadia profiles Rhodes; sees why the system failed Elise Marchetti; commitment hardens.
ACT 1 END — Nadia commits to finishing Rhodes; an anonymous message proves someone knows what she is.
Nadia hunts the message's source; first sign Rhodes is not a normal target.
Rhodes counters — smarter than past targets; he starts leaking pieces of Nadia's past to the press.
The network debates the risk; loyalty tested; a rule bends.
A network member is exposed / endangered; Nadia's method costs others, not just herself.
Nadia sets up a clean kill on Rhodes; meticulous prep.
The kill attempt is a trap — Rhodes wanted her to try; she barely escapes.
MIDPOINT — Nadia realizes Rhodes has a case file on her FIRST kill; hunter becomes hunted.
Nadia scrambles to find the file; her origin wound surfaces in fragments.
The network fractures — someone wants out or is compromised; trust breaks.
Nadia isolates the suspected leak; paranoia poisons the circle.
Nadia uncovers HOW Rhodes learned about her — a leak inside her own circle, confirmed.
Nadia strikes back, thinks she's cornered Rhodes.
ACT 2 END — false victory flips: Rhodes reveals her first-kill evidence is on a dead-man's-switch.
Nadia weighs the impossible choice; the cost of her war surfaces (origin fragments deepen, full reveal held for ch34).
Nadia must choose — kill Rhodes and trigger exposure, or let him live and stay hunted.
Nadia rebuilds trust with the loyal network members; a plan forms.
Nadia turns Rhodes's own method against him; hunts the dead-man's-switch; network reunites.
Final confrontation — earned through physical evidence, not confession; Rhodes dies, but not cleanly.
Aftermath; the podcast frames it as "justice served"; loose ends tied.
Case closes. Last beat: evidence about Nadia's first kill surfaces in someone else's hands. Book-2 hook — she's hunted, and this time it's personal.

38: Book 1 closes the Rhodes case: the man who walked free is finished, and the podcast frames it publicly as justice finally served. Nadia survives, her network mostly intact, her method proven. But she is no longer invisible — the two-way hunt cost her the one thing she guarded most: secrecy.

must_avoid: Unreliable narrator hiding the killing from the reader
Children in danger or on-page sexual violence
Flat stretches with no reveal or reversal for 4+ chapters
must_include_book: Anti-hero protagonist the reader knows is a killer from chapter 1
Guilty targets the system genuinely failed to punish
A hidden network of women, each with a distinct skill and risk
A two-way hunt: the antagonist figures out what she is
Origin wound (a loved one failed by the law) revealed gradually
Victories earned through competence and physical evidence, not confession
A network betrayal that hurts because loyalty was real
Book-1 case fully closed; series arc (the first kill) left as the ticking bomb
ending_book1: Book 1 closes the Rhodes case: the man who walked free is finished, and the podcast frames it publicly as justice finally served. Nadia survives, her network mostly intact, her method proven. But she is no longer invisible — the two-way hunt cost her the one thing she guarded most: secrecy.
hook_book2: The evidence Rhodes built about Nadia's very first kill did not die with him. In the final beat, it surfaces in someone else's hands — someone who doesn't want money or a story. They want Nadia to work for them. The hunter is now on a leash.
surface_plot: Reader thinks: Nadia Cole, a beloved investigative podcaster, reopens the unsolved murder of Elise Marchetti and hunts the powerful man who walked free. As she closes in, someone starts hunting her back — leaking her past, threatening her sources. A cat-and-mouse between a crusading journalist and a killer who covered his tracks.
true_plot: Actually: Nadia is not just investigating — she is the executioner, and the reader knows it from chapter 1. When the system fails, she engineers clean "accidents" and airtight frames. Her podcast is both cover and recruitment: a hidden network of women (a lawyer, a coroner, a hacker) feeds her what the courts ignore. Her new target isn't just guilty — he has figured out what she does and is quietly building the case that will expose her and unravel her network. The real question isn't whether she catches him. It's whether she can finish him before he finishes her — without her network, or her own buried first kill, coming to light.
